plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets turn lilac as these feathery-leaved trees drop clouds of trumpet-shaped blossoms. The flowers carpet pavements and parked cars in purple, so the tree seems to bloom twice: once overhead and once on the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-October to late November in the southern hemisphere spring, with the heaviest bloom in late October and November
plants.location: Pretoria and Johannesburg, South Africa, and Sydney, Australia
plants.funFact: Although the jacaranda is native to South America, Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. Its bloom comes so close to university exam season that local folklore says a flower landing on your head means you will pass.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens its silky, often lightly fragrant flowers just as autumn leaves are falling. Single and semi-double blooms with bright golden stamens appear in pink and white, and they attract late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late October into winter, peaking around mid-November in many gardens
plants.location: Gardens of the southeastern United States, such as the South Carolina Lowcountry, and its native Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed for an edible oil used in parts of East Asia.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Bare stems rise from the ground and carry spidery, ruffled pink flowers that sparkle in low autumn light. The flowers appear when most other perennials have faded, and they are tough enough to survive frosty weather.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to November, with flowers commonly opening in October and November in the northern hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens in the United Kingdom, including Scotland, and other temperate regions; native to South Africa
plants.funFact: The flowers come before the leaves, which emerge after the blooms fade. This is why the bulbs are often grown in sunny, sheltered spots at the base of a wall, where they get a baking summer and bloom reliably in autumn.
